exposure: Doppler ultrasound indices (umbilical artery S/D ratio, umbilical artery pulsatility index, middle cerebral artery pulsatility index, aortic isthmus flow index, ductus venosus waveform, umbilical vein waveform)
outcome: early neonatal morbidity (NICU admission, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, interventricular hemorrhage, necrotizing enterocolitis)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies with small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetuses, excluding those with chromosome abnormality, major organ anomaly, or intrauterine infection.
finding: The study found no significant correlation between MPI or Doppler ultrasound parameters and perinatal mortality or early neonatal morbidity in SGA fetuses, but identified gestational age (<38 wks) as the most significant factor associated with early neonatal morbidity.
cross-section timing: Measurements taken within 48 hours before delivery.
gest_age: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA); a significant factor was identified as GA <38 weeks.
